title: Nonzero fixed vectors for rational representations of smooth unipotent groups
statement: Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field] (every nonconstant polynomial over $K$ has a root in $K$). Let $U$ be a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] affine group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] over $K$. Assume that there are $m\geq1$ and a homomorphism of $K$-group schemes $i:U\to\operatorname{GL}_{m,K}$ [def-sc-general-linear-group] which is faithful: for every commutative $K$-algebra $R$ the map $i(R):U(R)\to\operatorname{GL}_m(R)$ is injective, where $U(R)$ denotes the morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}R\to U$ over $K$; and that for every $u\in U(K)$ the matrix $i(u)$ is unipotent: $(i(u)-I_m)^N=0$ for some integer $N\geq1$ depending on $u$. For every $d\geq1$ and every homomorphism of $K$-group schemes $\rho:U\to\operatorname{GL}_{d,K}$ (a rational representation on $K^d$), there exists $v\in K^d$ with $v\ne0$ such that $\rho(u)v=v$ for every $u\in U(K)$. Here $U(K)$ denotes the morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}K\to U$ over $K$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and the action is ordinary matrix multiplication on column vectors.

source.place: Corollary 3.35, printed p.75 (a homomorphism with trivial kernel, i.e. a faithful finite-dimensional representation, is a closed immersion); Corollary 14.12, printed p.283 (smooth groups and the geometric-matrix criterion); Proposition 14.3 and the definition in section 14.b, printed p.280 (every nonzero rational representation has a fixed vector); applied in the proof of Lemma 19.16, printed p.401.

proof.text: Fix $d\geq1$ and the given rational representation $\rho:U\to\operatorname{GL}_{d,K}$. For each $u\in U(K)$ apply [lem-sfb-rational-representation-unipotent-point] with $G=U$, $r=\rho$, and the faithful homomorphism $i$ in the hypothesis. Its field hypothesis holds since $K$ is algebraically closed, its affine finite-type hypotheses are part of the item, and its faithfulness is exactly injectivity on $R$-points for every commutative $K$-algebra $R$. The hypothesis $(i(u)-I_m)^N=0$ is given for this particular $u$. We obtain $(\rho(u)-I_d)^{M_u}=0$ for some $M_u\geq1$. This proves unipotence in the requested representation, not just in the original faithful one. No uniform exponent is needed.

source.place: Section 9.19, printed p.171; pointwise application of representation independence of unipotence.

proof.text: Let $H=\{\rho(u):u\in U(K)\}\subseteq\operatorname{GL}_d(K)$. The functor-of-points description in [def-sc-group-scheme] makes $U(K)$ a group and makes $\rho(K)$ a group homomorphism. The matrix description in [def-sc-general-linear-group] identifies its target with invertible matrices. Explicitly, $I_d=\rho(e)$, $\rho(u)\rho(w)=\rho(uw)$, and $\rho(u)^{-1}=\rho(u^{-1})$. Thus $H$ is a subgroup. By step 1 every $h\in H$ satisfies $(h-I_d)^N=0$ for some $N\geq1$: choose $u$ with $h=\rho(u)$ and take $N=M_u$.

source.place: Proposition 14.1, printed p.279: passage from a group action to its group of matrices.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-unipotent-matrix-group-fixed-vector] to $K$, $d$, and the subgroup $H$ from step 2. Its positive-dimension hypothesis is exactly $d\geq1$, and its pointwise unipotence hypothesis was verified in steps 1--2. It gives a nonzero $v\in K^d$ with $hv=v$ for every $h\in H$. For every $u\in U(K)$ the matrix $\rho(u)$ lies in $H$, so $\rho(u)v=v$. This is the asserted vector for the arbitrary $d$ and $\rho$.

source.place: Proposition 14.1, printed pp.279--280; equivalence with the fixed-vector definition of unipotent algebraic groups in section 14.b, printed p.280.

proof_origin.place: Section 9.19, printed p.171, followed by Proposition 14.1, printed pp.279--280. These provide the pointwise representation-independence input and the abstract common fixed-vector argument underlying section 14.b.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q47-5244c86b6 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and both new nodes in full. The item's statement is unchanged and its only citer, lem-sfb-general-linear-reductive step 4, still matches it. The proof has three steps. Step 1 cites lem-sfb-rational-representation-unipotent-point: G=U, r=rho and i keep the item's hypotheses verbatim, and the exponent M_u is allowed to depend on u. Step 2 is genuinely elementary: H=rho(U(K)) is a subgroup by the group-of-points description in def-sc-group-scheme and the matrix-group description in def-sc-general-linear-group. Step 3 cites lem-sfb-unipotent-matrix-group-fixed-vector, which gives one v fixed by all of H. New node 1 matches Milne iAG Theorem 9.18 (p.170) and 9.19 (p.171), read in the PDF: i(g_s)=i(g)_s=I, so g_s=e by injectivity of i on K-points, and then r(g)=r(g_u) is unipotent. Algebraically closed is a special case of Milne's perfect field, and no smoothness is needed. I tested it on G_m, on G_a in characteristic p and on mu_p. New node 2 is exactly Milne Prop. 14.1 (pp.279-280: an abstract group acting unipotently over any field, with footnote 1 for descending from the algebraic closure). I tested d=1, U_n and a cyclic group of order p, and noted that the hypothesis must hold for every element of H. Both new nodes are statement-only, self-contained and strictly smaller than the item; neither restates a clause of it. Searching snapshot/dag/nodes with rg -L (unipotent, kolchin, fixed vector, jordan decomposition) and the main-20261015 blueprint found no duplicate or generalization. No SGA citation and no cycle. Milne's own route goes through 14.10/14.12 and needs smoothness; the new pointwise route proves the same K-point conclusion without it. The item's smoothness hypothesis is therefore unused but kept, which does not weaken the target. No changes and no tool_uses.

lean.statement: theorem exists_nonzero_fixedVector_of_faithful_unipotent (K : Type u) [Field K] [IsAlgClosed K] (U : Over (Spec (.of K))) [GrpObj U] [IsAffine U.left] [Smooth U.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType U.hom] [QuasiCompact U.hom] (m : ℕ) (_hm : 1 ≤ m) (i : U ⟶ GeneralLinearGroup (ULift.{u} (Fin m)) K) [IsMonHom i] (_hfaithful : ∀ (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra K R], Function.Injective (fun x : (Spec (.of R)).asOver (Spec (.of K)) ⟶ U ↦ x ≫ i)) (_hunipotent : ∀ x : (Spec (.of K)).asOver (Spec (.of K)) ⟶ U, ∃ N : ℕ, 1 ≤ N ∧ ((GeneralLinearGroup.homMulEquiv (ULift.{u} (Fin m)) K K (x ≫ i)).val - 1) ^ N = 0) (d : ℕ) (_hd : 1 ≤ d) (ρ : U ⟶ GeneralLinearGroup (ULift.{u} (Fin d)) K) [IsMonHom ρ] : ∃ v : ULift.{u} (Fin d) → K, v ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ x : (Spec (.of K)).asOver (Spec (.of K)) ⟶ U, Matrix.mulVec (GeneralLinearGroup.homMulEquiv (ULift.{u} (Fin d)) K K (x ≫ ρ)).val v = v

reviewed_lean.note: Every clause matches the node: algebraically closed K; U over Spec K with GrpObj, IsAffine, Smooth, LocallyOfFiniteType and QuasiCompact; i into GL(ULift(Fin m)) K with IsMonHom; faithfulness as injectivity of x ↦ x≫i on R-points for all R : Type u (the universe is forced by upstream homMulEquiv and is equivalent to the node's condition for affine U); unipotence on K-points via homMulEquiv with an existential N ≥ 1 per point; arbitrary d ≥ 1 and ρ with IsMonHom; conclusion ∃ v ≠ 0 with mulVec v = v for every K-point, one v for all points.
